placements.why: This envelope's content is a database platform decision (PostgreSQL to QuantumDB) — an infrastructure/technical-systems choice. No strata category exists yet in this repo to hold architecture-grain organizational content, and nothing in Opportunity/Strategy/Product/Organization/Proof/Templates/Calibration territory (none of which exist either) plausibly covers a database migration; this is the first content requiring that category, so it is minted standalone per the NEW check.
placements.title: Technical infrastructure and system-design decisions
placements.frame: Does this content record a decision about the systems, platforms, or technologies the product runs on, as distinct from market strategy, product scope, or organizational process?

placements.title: Migration decisions declared first, justified and ratified after
placements.frame: When a technology migration is named, does the performance/cost rationale precede the decision or follow it as after-the-fact support, and who — speaker or formal document — is doing the ratifying?
placements.why: All three segments feed one recurring subject: a technology migration (PostgreSQL to QuantumDB) is declared as already underway (src-1), backed by flat performance/cost claims offered as justification rather than deliberation (src-2), and then re-presented as a ratified plan with a timeline in a formal memo (src-3). This is a directional theme — decision, rationale, ratification — that future envelopes about technology-migration choices will keep feeding, not a one-time fact; the 10x/licensing figures are evidence for this theme, not leaves of their own (grain-test: a measurement joins supporting_segments, it does not mint). No existing leaf exists in this empty graph to hold it, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Architecture stratum.
